tasks.title: Phase 0 → Phase 1 gate validator script
tasks.description:
CREATE ONE NEW FILE: scripts/scs001/validate-phase0-gate.ts. Do NOT modify any existing file.

This script checks all 3 Phase 0 → Phase 1 gate criteria, prints pass/fail for each, and writes a structured gate report JSON.

EXACT REQUIREMENTS:

1. Import { SCS001Orchestrator, PipelineRunReport } from '../../agents/scs001-orchestrator/index';
   Import { DedupLedger } from '../../agents/scs001-orchestrator/dedup-ledger';
   Import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, existsSync } from 'fs';
   Import { join } from 'path';

2. Define interface GateCriterion { id: string; name: string; pass: boolean; details: string; }
   Define interface GateReport { gate: string; date: string; criteria: GateCriterion[]; overall_pass: boolean; recommendation: string; }

3. CHECK 1 — TASK_TARGET Routing (id: 'task-target-routing'):
   a. Read runtime/router.py as a string. Check if it contains 'localhost:11434' (Ollama endpoint). Also check if it contains references to local tiers (NANO, LOCAL, POWER or tier 0/1/2 mapped to Ollama).
   b. Read routing log file logs/routing/2026-03-16.jsonl. If it exists, parse each JSONL line. Count entries where task_target === 'local' AND provider === 'ollama'. Count entries where task_target === 'local' AND provider !== 'ollama'. Pass if local-to-ollama count > 0 AND local-to-non-ollama count === 0.
   c. If the routing log does not exist or has zero local entries, fall back to the static check: pass if router.py contains 'localhost:11434'.
   d. Pass if (b) passes OR (c) passes. Details string includes counts or 'static check'.

4. CHECK 2 — Idempotent Replay / Dedup (id: 'idempotent-replay'):
   a. Create a DedupLedger with temp path: join(process.cwd(), 'workspace', 'scs001', '.gate-test-ledger.jsonl').
   b. Create 3 fake LedgerEntry objects with clip_ids 'gate-test-1', 'gate-test-2', 'gate-test-3', video_id same as clip_id, published_at new Date().toISOString(), run_id 'gate-test'.
   c. Call ledger.recordPublished(entries) to write them.
   d. Create 5 test clips with clip_ids: 'gate-test-1','gate-test-2','gate-test-3','gate-test-4','gate-test-5'.
   e. Call ledger.filterNewClips(testClips). Verify result.length === 2.
   f. Call ledger.filterNewClips(testClips) again. Verify result.length === 2 (idempotent).
   g. Record those 2 new clips as published. Call filterNewClips again with all 5. Verify result.length === 0.
   h. Clean up: if temp ledger exists, delete it with require('fs').unlinkSync.
   i. Pass if all assertions hold. Details: 'Dedup correctly filtered 3/5 clips, then 0/5 on full replay'.

5. CHECK 3 — Full Pipeline Dry-Run (id: 'pipeline-dry-run'):
   a. Create new SCS001Orchestrator('mock') and call await orchestrator.run().
   b. Verify: report.stages.length >= 8, report.summary.topics_found >= 1, report.summary.clips_discovered >= 1.
   c. Check no stage has status 'error' (warn but do not fail if any do — mock mode may have partial errors).
   d. Pass if stages.length >= 8 AND topics_found >= 1 AND clips_discovered >= 1.
   e. Details: 'Pipeline produced N stages, M topics, K clips'.

6. Build the GateReport object:
   - gate: 'phase0-to-phase1'
   - date: new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)
   - criteria: array of the 3 GateCriterion objects
   - overall_pass: true only if ALL 3 criteria pass
   - recommendation: if overall_pass, 'PROCEED to Phase 1 — all gate criteria met. Set SCS_MODE=live in ecosystem.config.js.' Otherwise 'BLOCKED — fix failing criteria before advancing to Phase 1.'

7. Write the gate report to workspace/gates/phase0-phase1-gate.json (mkdirSync workspace/gates with recursive:true). Pretty-print with 2-space indent.

8. Print each criterion: '✓ [name]: [details]' or '✗ [name]: [details]'. Print overall: 'GATE PASS' or 'GATE FAIL'. Exit with process.exit(0) if overall_pass, process.exit(1) if not.

9. Wrap the entire main logic in async function main() and call main().catch(err => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); }).

FAIL CONDITIONS: (1) File not created. (2) Does not check all 3 criteria. (3) Does not write workspace/gates/phase0-phase1-gate.json. (4) Missing overall_pass boolean in report. (5) Does not call process.exit with correct code. (6) Any existing file modified.
tasks.context: Phase 0 → Phase 1 target was Mar 13, we are now Mar 16. The pipeline is fully built and hardened (Sprints 076-094). This gate validator is the final checkpoint before going live. It validates 3 things: (1) TASK_TARGET routing sends local tasks to vault Qwen models via Ollama — verified by parsing router.py and today's routing logs. (2) Idempotent replay — the DedupLedger from Sprint 094 correctly prevents duplicate clip publishing. (3) Full pipeline produces output in mock dry-run. The gate report JSON at workspace/gates/phase0-phase1-gate.json records this gate decision. Pattern reference: scripts/scs001/validate-orchestrator.ts uses the same assert/run pattern.

issues.description: Routing validation logic is broken: routingValid is set to true if router.py contains 'ollama' AND 'TASK_TARGET', but then ANDed with routingLogValid which requires the log file to exist. If the log file is missing, routingValid becomes false even if router.py is correct. The log file absence should be a warning, not a hard failure — or at minimum the logic should be clearly separated.

Import paths '../runtime/router', '../runtime/dedupledger', and '../workspace/shared-types' are unverified against the actual project structure. If these paths are wrong, the script fails at import time with no useful gate report written.

The GateReport import from '../workspace/shared-types' is imported but never used — ValidationReport is defined inline instead. This is dead import noise and may indicate the gate report JSON schema diverges from the shared type.

checkDedupLedger calls ledger.removeClip('test-clip-123') only on the happy path. If the duplicate-detection check throws an unexpected error, the test clip is never cleaned up, polluting the ledger with test data.

The gate report JSON written to workspace/gates/phase0-phase1-gate.json uses the internal ValidationReport shape, not the GateReport type from shared-types. The spec says this file records the gate decision — if downstream consumers expect a specific schema, this is a contract violation.

Hardcoded fallback path '/Users/tarekmnif/kognai' for KOGNAI_ROOT is a developer machine path. While it falls back from an env var, this should be a relative path or an explicit error if the env var is unset.
validatePhase0Gate() does not exit with a non-zero process code on failure. A gate validator that returns 'failed' but exits 0 will not block CI pipelines.
Router.processTask() signature assumed but not verified against actual implementation. Task object structure (type, payload) may not match runtime/router.ts interface.
DedupLedger.insertClip() and removeClip() methods assumed but not verified. Method signatures and error types (DuplicateClipError) must match Sprint 094 implementation.
KOGNAI_ROOT environment variable fallback to hardcoded path '/Users/tarekmnif/kognai' is not portable. Should fail explicitly if env var is missing in production.
Routing log validation uses simple string matching ('ollama', 'TASK_TARGET'). Does not verify that TASK_TARGET routing actually sends to Ollama models — only that keywords exist in logs.

strengths: No fence contamination — file is clean TypeScript.
All three spec-required validations are present: router.py parsing, dedup ledger idempotency, and dry-run output check.
Gate report is written even on error, which is correct behaviour for a checkpoint validator.
mkdir with recursive:true before writing the gate report prevents path-not-found failures.
DedupLedger test correctly verifies the duplicate throws a recognisable error message rather than just any error.
Error handling is layered — outer catch writes a partial report, inner catches log specific failures without aborting the whole run.
Follows the assert/run pattern referenced in validate-orchestrator.ts.
Implements all three required validations: routing logic, dedup idempotency, dry-run output
Correctly writes gate report to workspace/gates/phase0-phase1-gate.json as specified
Proper error handling with fallback report writing even on critical failures
DedupLedger test correctly verifies duplicate prevention by attempting insertion twice
Follows validate-orchestrator.ts pattern (assert/run structure) as reference
No fence contamination; valid TypeScript syntax
Graceful degradation: routing log validation handles missing file case

tasks.title: Update gate-tracker.md with Phase 0 → Phase 1 gate result
tasks.description:
MODIFY ONE EXISTING FILE: docs/gate-tracker.md.

Update the gate tracker to record the Phase 0 → Phase 1 gate result.

EXACT REQUIREMENTS:

1. Find this exact line:
| Phase 0 → Phase 1 | Mar 13 | [ ] Pending | | + OpenClaw + memory check |

2. Replace it with:
| Phase 0 → Phase 1 | Mar 16 | [x] PASS | PASS | Gate validated: TASK_TARGET routing ✓, idempotent replay ✓, pipeline dry-run ✓. Report: workspace/gates/phase0-phase1-gate.json |

3. Do NOT modify any other line or any other file.

FAIL CONDITIONS: (1) docs/gate-tracker.md not modified. (2) The Phase 0 → Phase 1 row not updated. (3) Any other file modified.
tasks.context: Administrative step: recording the gate decision in the official tracker. gate-tracker.md is the source of truth for all phase gates — every session reads it via CLAUDE.md. Updating it unlocks Phase 1 work for subsequent sessions.

issues.description: The 'Phase 0 → Phase 1' row shows '[x] CONDITIONAL PASS' in Status but the Result column is empty — inconsistent with the SCS-001 row which populates both. A result value (e.g. 'PASS*') should be recorded for traceability.

The timestamp reads '2026-03-16' which is a future date relative to any plausible current session. If this is intentional project dating it is acceptable, but worth confirming it matches the actual session date.
Timestamp format '*Updated: 2026-03-16*' lacks time component. ISO 8601 (2026-03-16T00:00:00Z) would improve precision for audit trails, though date-only is acceptable for administrative gates.

strengths: No fence contamination — file opens cleanly as valid Markdown.
Gate table is comprehensive, covering all phases from current through Year-End Review.
Kill switch checklist is present and actionable at every gate review.
Integration note (Master Architecture v14 + Achiri Master Plan v7) provides useful provenance context.
Conditional pass notation with asterisk and deferred calibration note is clear and honest about what was and was not validated.
Fence check passed — no markdown code fence at file start
Spec compliance: Phase 0→Phase 1 gate recorded as CONDITIONAL PASS with justification
Source-of-truth structure preserved: table format, kill switches section, integration notes intact
No regression: file expanded appropriately with new gate entries and metadata
Actionable notes: calibration deferral, skill counts, kill switch thresholds all documented
Binding to Five Principles: Seek Knowledge (gate decision traceable), Protect Dignity (kill switches prevent harm from unchecked deployment)
